newsitem.title: FRANCE: Strafor sees 1996 profit of 200 mln Ffr.
newsitem.headline: Strafor sees 1996 profit of 200 mln Ffr.

text.p: French business equipment supplier Strafor-Facom expects to report a net attributable profit of around 200 million francs in 1996 and increase its results next year, chairman Henri Lachmann said in an interview on Tuesday.

For 1996, "analysts generally expect a net attributable profit of around 200 million francs. I think we will reach that," he told the newspaper La Tribune. "For the group as a whole, that means a result of between 250 and 260 million francs, compared with 182 million last year."
Turnover this year is expected to rise around six percent to just under nine billion francs, he said.
Next year, "our turnover could rise around five percent on a like-for-like basis. We expect to significantly increase our profit," Lachmann said.
He said the sale of Strafor's Bongard bakery equipment subsidiary announced on Monday should help reduce debt by around 150 million francs and generate a small capital gain.

"Part of this sale will be paid in cash, around 85 million francs, and the rest in convertible bonds," he said. Strafor expects to reduce debt by 350 million francs this year, using 200 million of free cash flow and the Bongard sale proceeds, to bring the debt-to-equity ratio to below one, Lachmann said.
He said the group planned to reduce its participation in Manoir Industries to below 50 percent, and that operation would help cut debt by 500 million francs next year.
"By the end of 1998, our debt should represent just half our equity," he said. In 1998, the group has the option to convert 500 million in convertible bonds, he said.
Lachmann said the Bongard sale was part of the group's strategy to focus on its core businesses, expand its share of the office equipment market in Germany and grow in the United States.
"We've decided to expand our partnership with U.S. firm Steelcase to cover new products and new regions," he said.
